title: Kinematics
summary: Describing motion with displacement, velocity and acceleration: motion graphs, the suvat equations for uniform acceleration, and projectile motion with and without air resistance.

keyterms.definition: The change in position of an object in a stated direction; a vector, measured in metres.
The total length of path travelled; a scalar, so it ignores direction.
Rate of change of displacement, v = Δs/Δt; a vector measured in m s⁻¹.
Rate of change of distance travelled; the magnitude of velocity for straight-line motion.
Rate of change of velocity, a = Δv/Δt; a vector measured in m s⁻².
Acceleration that is constant in magnitude and direction; the condition for using the suvat equations.
Motion under gravity alone, with no air resistance; acceleration g ≈ 9.8 m s⁻² downwards near Earth.
An object launched into the air and moving under gravity, with independent horizontal and vertical motion.
The constant velocity reached when drag balances weight, so the resultant force and acceleration are zero.
The velocity of one object as measured by an observer moving with another: v_AB = v_A − v_B.
The velocity at one moment, equal to the gradient of the tangent to a displacement–time graph.
Total displacement divided by total time taken.

questions.prompt: A runner completes exactly one lap of a 400 m track in 80 s. What are her average speed and average velocity?
questions.explanation: Average speed uses distance (400 m / 80 s = 5 m s⁻¹). After one full lap the displacement is zero, so the average velocity is zero.
Speed is a scalar: it has magnitude only. Velocity is the corresponding vector.

questions.text: The gradient of a velocity–time graph gives the ___.
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, so it is the gradient of a v–t graph.

questions.prompt: What does the area under a velocity–time graph represent?
questions.explanation: Area = velocity × time, which is displacement. Areas below the time axis count as negative displacement.

questions.prompt: Match each graph feature to the quantity it gives.
questions.explanation: Gradients give rates of change; areas under graphs give the accumulated quantity.

questions.prompt: A displacement–time graph for a car is a straight line with a negative gradient. The car is moving with
options: constant velocity in the negative direction
questions.explanation: A straight s–t line means constant velocity; a negative gradient means the velocity is in the negative direction.

questions.statement: An object can have a velocity of zero and a non-zero acceleration at the same instant.
questions.explanation: A ball thrown upwards is momentarily at rest at the top, but its acceleration is still g downwards.

questions.text: A car changes velocity from 12 m s⁻¹ to 30 m s⁻¹ in 6.0 s. Its average acceleration is ___ m s⁻².

questions.prompt: Train A moves east at 25 m s⁻¹ and train B moves east at 15 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of A relative to B?
questions.explanation: v_AB = v_A − v_B = 25 − 15 = 10 m s⁻¹ east: a passenger on B sees A pulling ahead.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to find instantaneous velocity from a curved s–t graph.
items: Choose the instant on the time axis
Draw a tangent to the curve at that point
Read two well-separated points on the tangent
questions.explanation: The instantaneous velocity is the gradient of the tangent at that time; using widely spaced points reduces reading error.

lessons.title: Uniform acceleration and the suvat equations

questions.prompt: Which condition must hold for the equations v = u + at and s = ut + ½at² to be valid?
questions.explanation: The suvat equations are derived assuming uniform (constant) acceleration.

questions.text: A stone is dropped from rest. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², its speed after 2.0 s is ___ m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at 2.0 m s⁻² for 5.0 s. How far does it travel?

questions.statement: In the absence of air resistance, a heavy ball and a light ball dropped together from the same height land at the same time.
questions.explanation: In free fall all objects have the same acceleration g, independent of mass.

questions.prompt: A cyclist moving at 8.0 m s⁻¹ brakes uniformly to rest in 16 m. What is the deceleration?
questions.explanation: v² = u² + 2as gives 0 = 64 + 2a(16), so a = −2.0 m s⁻²: a deceleration of 2.0 m s⁻².

questions.text: A ball thrown vertically upwards has, at its highest point, a vertical velocity of ___.
questions.explanation: At the top the vertical velocity changes sign, so it is momentarily zero, while the acceleration is still g downwards.

questions.prompt: Match each equation to the variable it does not contain.
questions.explanation: Pick the suvat equation that omits the quantity you neither know nor need.

questions.statement: A falling skydiver reaches terminal velocity when her weight becomes zero.
questions.explanation: Her weight stays the same. Terminal velocity is reached when drag grows to equal the weight, so the resultant force is zero.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown straight up at 14.7 m s⁻¹ (g = 9.8 m s⁻², no air resistance). How long until it returns to the thrower’s hand?
questions.explanation: Time to the top = u/g = 14.7/9.8 = 1.5 s; the motion is symmetric so the total time is 3.0 s.

questions.prompt: Order the stages of a skydiver’s fall before opening the parachute.
questions.explanation: As speed increases so does drag, reducing the resultant force and acceleration until they reach zero.

questions.prompt: Ignoring air resistance, which quantity stays constant during the flight of a projectile?
questions.explanation: Gravity acts only vertically, so with no air resistance there is no horizontal force and the horizontal velocity is constant.

questions.statement: The horizontal and vertical motions of a projectile can be analysed independently.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular components of motion are independent; they share only the time of flight.

questions.prompt: A ball is rolled horizontally off a table 1.25 m high at 3.0 m s⁻¹ (g = 10 m s⁻²). How far from the table does it land?
questions.explanation: Fall time: 1.25 = ½(10)t², so t = 0.50 s. Horizontal distance = 3.0 × 0.50 = 1.5 m.

questions.text: A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. Its initial vertical velocity component is ___ m s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: u_y = u sin θ = 20 × sin 30° = 10 m s⁻¹. The horizontal component is 20 cos 30° ≈ 17.3 m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: Without air resistance, which launch angle gives the maximum range on level ground?
questions.explanation: Range = u² sin 2θ / g, which is greatest when sin 2θ = 1, i.e. θ = 45°.

questions.statement: At the highest point of its path, a projectile launched at an angle has zero velocity.
questions.explanation: Only the vertical component is zero at the top; the horizontal component is still present.

questions.prompt: How does air resistance change the trajectory of a projectile compared with the ideal case?
options: Range and maximum height both decrease, and the path is no longer symmetric
Range increases but maximum height decreases
The path stays a symmetric parabola but is shorter
Only the time of flight changes
questions.explanation: Drag removes energy and opposes motion, so the projectile goes less high and less far, and the descent is steeper than the ascent.

questions.text: Two balls leave a cliff at the same moment: one dropped, one thrown horizontally. Ignoring air resistance, they hit the level ground below ___.
questions.explanation: Both have zero initial vertical velocity and the same vertical acceleration g, so their fall times are equal.

questions.prompt: Match each feature of ideal projectile motion.
questions.explanation: In ideal projectile motion only the vertical velocity changes, at a constant rate g.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to find the range of a projectile launched from level ground.
items: Resolve the launch velocity into components
Use the vertical motion to find the time of flight
Multiply horizontal velocity by time of flight
questions.explanation: Time links the two independent components: find it from the vertical motion, then use it horizontally.
